rv.q: This “La Sonnambula” would have been worth cheering for the singing alone.

Riccardo Frizza’s fluid conducting drew out the score’s long bel canto lines and limned its propulsive rhythmic structure, and his flexible support of the singers made every aria and ensemble breathe and soar.
This cast made that substantial and often glorious.
The concept is an interesting one that brings politics to the fore, but the execution is messy at best.

cn.t: Critics praise Nadine Sierra's spectacular vocal performance in the Met's new "La Sonnambula," but reviews are divided on the production itself, with some finding the staging disappointing despite strong singing.
